text: A decorator that takes its own arguments needs one extra layer — a function that returns a decorator.
repeat takes the number of times, then returns the actual decorator inside it.
That inner decorator wraps your function, and the wrapper runs it repeatedly.
[chuckle] So it's three nested functions: one for the argument, one for the function, one for the call.
[sniff] The at-repeat with times equals three means greet now runs three times on every call.
So a single greet call prints the greeting three times, controlled by the decorator's argument.
[sigh] Notice the wraps decorator from functools — it copies the original function's name and docs onto the wrapper.
Without it, greet's name would wrongly show as wrapper, confusing debuggers and documentation tools.
[groan] Parameterized decorators power real frameworks — think route paths, retry counts, and cache sizes.
